headline: NEXGEN BREAKS GROUND ON $2.2B ROOK I: Athabasca Uranium Mine Targets 30M lbs/yr — Construction Starts After March Federal Approval
snippet: NexGen Energy Ltd. (TSX: NXE) broke ground August 13 on its C$2.2 billion Rook I Project in the southwestern Athabasca Basin — launching a four-year construction timeline for what is designed to become one of the world's largest and lowest-cost uranium mines, targeting 30 million pounds of annual production from the Arrow Deposit by late 2030. The groundbreaking was attended by Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe, former Prime Minister Stephen Harper, and investor Kevin O'Leary, signaling broad political and capital-market consensus after NexGen received its final federal approval in March 2026. For uranium investors, this is the most consequential new Western supply event of the decade: Rook I will add more Canadian uranium production capacity than any project since McArthur River, entering a market at $87/lb where no comparable-scale alternative exists in the global development pipeline.

headline: SLAM EXPLORATION DRILLS 1.19% CuEq OVER 24.6m AT GOODWIN, DISCOVERS MASSIVE SULPHIDES 2,000m NW — Bathurst Camp Footprint Expands
source_name: Junior Mining Network / SLAM Exploration Ltd. (TSX-V: SXL)
snippet: SLAM Exploration Ltd. (TSX-V: SXL) reported August 14 that hole GW26-29 at the Goodwin copper-nickel-cobalt project in New Brunswick's Bathurst Mining Camp returned 24.6 metres grading 1.19% copper equivalent from the massive sulphide zone — and simultaneously disclosed that hole GW26-36 discovered new massive sulphides 2,000 metres northwest of the Logan zone, materially extending the system's potential footprint. SLAM has completed 2,600 metres across 12 holes (37% of the 7,000-metre 2026 program) with 992 samples submitted for multi-element assay; the 2,000-metre step-out discovery adds a district-scale dimension to a CuNiCo system being tested against the ovoid geometry of the Bathurst Camp's historically largest deposits.

headline: TOWER RESOURCES: 18.8m AT 2.57 g/t Au + 43 g/t HIGH-GRADE SKIN AT RABBIT NORTH BC — Plus Porphyry Cu-Au Breccia Pipe Discovery
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Tower Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: TWR)
snippet: Tower Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: TWR) reported August 13 that hole 074 at Rabbit North near Kamloops, B.C. intersected 18.8 metres at 2.57 g/t gold in the Thunder zone — including a 0.7-metre interval of 43 g/t gold — while hole 075 hit an unexpected Rainbow porphyry breccia pipe returning 5.3 metres at 0.71 g/t Au and 0.38% Cu plus 22.6 metres at 0.56 g/t Au and 0.35% Cu from an 8-hole, 2,303.5-metre June program. The Rainbow porphyry pipe discovery is the more significant long-term finding: porphyry Cu-Au systems in the Kamloops belt typically underpin materially larger resource bases than the epithermal gold zones that sit above them, and Tower has now demonstrated both target types coexist at Rabbit North.

headline: P2 GOLD HITS 79.25m OF 0.78 g/t Au + 0.29% Cu AT LUCKY STRIKE NEVADA — High-Grade Core Thickening Southwest Ahead of Q4 2026 Feasibility
source_name: Junior Mining Network / P2 Gold Inc. (TSX-V: PGLD)
snippet: P2 Gold Inc. (TSX-V: PGLD) reported August 12 that ten reverse-circulation holes at the Lucky Strike Zone of its Gabbs gold-copper project in Nevada returned a best result of 79.25 metres at 0.78 g/t gold and 0.29% copper — including a 21.34-metre high-grade core at 1.28 g/t Au and 0.34% Cu — with the highest-grading gold-copper core visibly thickening as infill drilling steps southwest, building toward the Q4 2026 resource update and feasibility study. P2 Gold has now completed 78 RC holes at Gabbs since October 2025, and the consistent Lucky Strike geometry — thick, near-surface gold-copper mineralization widening in the highest-grade zone — is the structural foundation that a large open-pit feasibility study requires.

headline: CATL'S JIANXIAWO LIMBO CRASHED LITHIUM 30% FROM MAY PEAK — 4% of Global Supply Idle as China Futures Market Whipsaws on Restart Speculation
snippet: A year after CATL idled its flagship Jianxiawo lithium mine — representing roughly 4% of global supply — persistent uncertainty over whether the operation will restart is driving wild swings in China's nascent lithium futures market, contributing to a nearly 30% price decline since May's peak as traders swing between surplus and deficit scenarios on unverified restart rumours. For junior lithium investors, the Jianxiawo situation illustrates why the lithium price recovery story is hostage to Chinese operator behaviour: one idled Chinese mine has more immediate price impact than the combined output of most development-stage projects globally, and the structural bifurcation between low-cost brine producers (Cauchari-Olaroz at $5,600/t) and high-cost hard-rock operations will continue widening until a definitive production decision from CATL removes the uncertainty premium from the market.

headline: FIRST MINING GOLD Q2: $40.5M CASH, SPRINGPOLE FEDERAL EA APPROVED — Ontario's Largest Undeveloped Gold Deposit Clears Final Regulatory Gate
source_name: First Mining Gold Corp. (TSX: FF) / Stock Titan
snippet: First Mining Gold Corp. (TSX: FF) reported August 12 its Q2 2026 results with $40.5 million in cash and marketable securities — headlined by the federal environmental assessment approval for Springpole, Ontario's largest undeveloped gold deposit, which clears the final major regulatory hurdle before permitting and construction planning can begin. The Springpole EA approval is the milestone that has been blocking First Mining's path to a construction decision for years; combined with continued drilling at Duparquet and Indigenous partnership progress, it repositions First Mining as a primary pre-construction gold development vehicle at a gold price where Springpole's economics are compelling.

headline: UBS GOLD TARGET $5,000 BY H1 2027: Lower Real Rates + Sovereign Demand + Weak Dollar — Mining Stocks Still Single-Digit PE Versus Record Margins
snippet: UBS strategists set a $5,000 per ounce gold target for H1 2027 in commentary coinciding with gold's August 13 pullback from near $4,500 to the $4,349 range on tame PPI data — arguing the selloff confirms a higher-low formation rather than a trend reversal, with falling real rates, a structurally weaker dollar, and consistent central bank sovereign demand providing the three-pillar foundation for the next leg higher. The valuation gap that makes the UBS thesis actionable for equity investors: gold mining stocks are still trading at single-digit forward PE multiples despite generating record operating margins at $4,300+ gold, a disconnect that the bank argues will close through sector re-rating before the $5,000 target is tested.

headline: GRANDE PORTAGE HITS 49% ON 2026 ALASKA DRILL, PIVOTS TO MINE DEVELOPMENT DATA — 100% WARRANTS EXERCISED, C$1.5M ADDED
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Grande Portage Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: GPG)
snippet: Grande Portage Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: GPG) announced August 13 that 1,605 of 3,255 planned metres (49%) have been completed at the New Amalga Gold Project in southeast Alaska, with the 2026 program explicitly pivoting from resource expansion to collecting hydrogeological and geotechnical data required for mine design — alongside confirmation that 100% of the 6.0 million outstanding warrants were exercised by shareholders at C$0.25 ahead of their August 12 expiry, generating C$1.5 million in additional proceeds. The 100% warrant exercise is the shareholder-sentiment signal: existing holders voluntarily adding C$1.5M to the treasury as the project crosses from exploration into pre-development is the kind of organic conviction indicator that precedes institutional attention in small-cap gold developers.
